option.name: text
option.value: This is an educational Android project called Howest Desserts. Package: be.howest.henrique.howestdesserts. Use Kotlin. Use Jetpack Compose. Do not create XML layouts. Prefer simple, readable code for students new to Android. Do not add a library without first explaining why it is required. Use the existing Gradle version catalog. Use a ViewModel as the screen-level state holder. Expose screen state with StateFlow. Prefer state down and events up. Do not add Retrofit, Room or Navigation. Do not introduce repositories, dependency injection or a domain layer. Explain significant generated code. Do not modify unrelated files.

option.name: text
option.value:
Create a Kotlin data class Dessert that matches this JSON object: {"id": 0, "productName": "Cupcake", "imageFile": "https://...", "description": "...", "size": 500, "price": 5.0}. Explain each field and why a data class is used.
Which dependencies do I need for Coil AsyncImage with remote image URLs, viewModel() in Compose and collectAsStateWithLifecycle()? Explain why each one is required and how to add them to the version catalog.
Create a DessertViewModel and a DessertUiState that expose a hardcoded List<Dessert> using StateFlow. Explain the difference between MutableStateFlow and StateFlow.
Create a DessertRoute composable that collects the ui state with collectAsStateWithLifecycle() and passes the desserts to a stateless DessertListScreen. Explain what “state down, events up” means here.
Create a reusable Material 3 DessertCard with Coil AsyncImage that shows the image, product name, stock and price, and a DessertListScreen with a two-column LazyVerticalGrid.
Create a reusable, stateless DessertDetailScreen that shows one Dessert: image, product name, description, size and price. Add a @Preview. Do not use Navigation Compose.
Explain this Kotlin error: “Argument type mismatch: actual type is ‘String’, but ‘Int’ was expected” when creating a data class instance.
